title: HE RAN.
paragraphs: Because he was strong enough to leave.

The room was quiet.
The doors were closed.
The opportunity was perfect.

Joseph was young, strong, and far from home.
No family watching.
No synagogue nearby.
No accountability group.
Just him… and the wife of Potiphar.

Not once.
Not casually.
Daily pressure.
Daily seduction.

The kind that melts discipline.
The kind that makes secrets feel safe.
But Joseph carried something stronger than desire.
So he said something that echoes across centuries:

“How then can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?”
— Genesis 39:9
Then one day the trap snapped shut.

The house empty.
The door closed.
Her hand gripping his cloak.
For a moment the world held its breath.

Left the cloak.
Left the reputation.
Left the comfort.
Because sometimes obedience looks like loss… before it becomes promotion.
Years later the prisoner would become prime minister.
The fugitive from temptation would save nations from famine.
And the man who ran from sin would run an empire.
Victory over temptation doesn’t always look heroic.
Because holiness is not proven by how long you stand near temptation…
But by how fast you flee it.
And here is the deeper truth.
At the cross, Jesus Christ carried the guilt of every secret failure, every hidden compromise, every moment we didn’t run.
The cross is where shame loses its grip.
His mercy is faster than your past.
Someone scrolling tonight needs the courage to leave temptation behind.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
